$comment: ADAAAA-7767 - frame-derived ground truth for a rights-cleared american-football broadcast. Labels were read from the pixels only: the broadcast score bug (two teal score boxes, one per team, plus period/clock) was read at 1 fps from native frames, and a scoring instant is the first frame whose score digits show the new value. No label comes from decide reason text, from a detection model's output, or from a soccer/basketball clip. Every instant is reported with the bracket it was narrowed to; several brackets are +-5 s rather than +-1 s because the community-access operator updates the bug a few seconds after the play (recorded per event in labelConfidence).

video.rights_holder: Belmont Media Center (producing community-access station; uploader access@belmontmedia.org)
video.attribution: Belmont Media Center, Belmont HS Boys Varsity Football: Marauders vs Westford, 2023-09-21, CC0 1.0, via the Internet Archive
video.audio: aac, commentary + crowd + PA whistle bed (the reason this clip is usable for the audio-trigger measurement)
video.frame_source: native 854x480 frames decoded at 1 fps; the score bug band (source y 400-446) was cropped per frame and read at native resolution
video.label_method: score-bug catalogue: 1 fps crops of the two score boxes (source x 243-288 and 462-508, y 409-436) read visually from native frames, bracketed by 4-row strips at 2-60 s steps until the transition was pinned; the instant is the first 1 fps frame showing the new digits. Non-event windows lie strictly inside a score-stable interval and were read at both ends.
video.label_confidence_note: The score bug is updated by the host operator a few seconds after the play, so an instant is the BUG UPDATE, not the snap-to-score moment; each event records the bracket it was narrowed to. A ±5 s label error is bounded by the brackets below, and the audio harness is scored with a widened -6 s/+3 s match window for that reason (see evals/american_football_val/audio-labels.json).
video.bug_anomaly: The bug displayed Westford 14 at halftime (first read at t=3800) while every third-quarter read shows 13. The half-time value is an operator entry error: the +2 at t~3795 is a two-point conversion / extra-point entry that was corrected to 13 before the third quarter. Recorded rather than silently repaired, and relevant to the corroboration-oracle follow-on: this score bug is NOT a trustworthy oracle for football.

segment.note: the whole rights-cleared recording is the clip: one continuous community-access broadcast of one game (pregame overlay, four quarters, halftime). The clip carries 11 verified scoring plays across 8391 s, which clears the >= 5 min / >= 6 scoring plays floor with the real count stated rather than a padded one.

coverage.note: Football scoring is sparse, which is why the clip is the whole game rather than a 5-minute slice: a 5-minute slice of this game holds at most one scoring play. The real count (11) is stated; nothing was padded to reach the floor.

evidence: 574 s after E01; end of Q2 (bug clock 0:21)
two plays apart from E02, so the TD and the XP are separate labelled scoring plays
1 fps band frames 3788 (7-12) and 3800 (7-14, bug state HALF 0:01)
delta 2 read at the half-time graphic; the third-quarter bug shows 13, so this entry was corrected by the operator (see video.bug_anomaly)
the TD/XP pair E07/E08 is 42 s apart
1 fps band frames 7405 (14-19/25 boundary read at 7420) and 7420 (14-25)
final score 20-26 confirmed at t=8150/8300; no extra point followed in the bug
score bug 0-0 at 800 and 824 (read in the 1000 s bracket: 0-0 at 1000)
24 s window inside the score-stable 0-0 interval (300-1608)
end-of-game handshake window, scored as a dead-ball window

known_gaps: No frame-level detection (box) slice was labelled for american football in this pass, so evals/detect_precision.py --backend florence has no american-football label space to score yet; evals/american_football_val/detect_val.jsonl is therefore absent rather than fabricated.
No american-football track manifest exists, so evals/track_metrics.py was not run for this type.

The score bug is not an oracle: it showed 14 at half time and 13 in the third quarter (video.bug_anomaly). Any future corroboration-oracle work must not assume overlay OCR is trustworthy on community-access football.
